stem: Andrew is 14 years old and has chronic severe asthma. He has frequent hospital admissions, exercise-induced symptoms, and nocturnal symptoms most days. He uses salbutamol most days. He has been prescribed salbutamol and fluticasone via a large-volume spacer but does not take the medication regularly because he hates the spacer. Which alternative delivery device would be most appropriate for him?

options.text: Metered dose inhaler (MDI) with a small-volume spacer

explanation: In a 14-year-old who can use inhaler devices and dislikes a spacer, a dry powder device is an appropriate alternative. Nebulisers with face masks are generally reserved for younger children or those unable to use handheld inhalers effectively. Oral salbutamol is not recommended for routine asthma management.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part B

rationale: The original item was a multiple-answer question. To make it a single-best-answer, it was rewritten to ask for the most appropriate alternative device. At age 14, a dry powder inhaler is a reasonable spacer-free option.

optionExplanations.A: Could be used in some children, but it still requires a spacer, which he dislikes.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: a dry powder device is suitable for an adolescent who can generate adequate inspiratory flow and may improve adherence if he dislikes a spacer.
optionExplanations.C: Not the best choice for a cooperative 14-year-old who can use a handheld inhaler device.
optionExplanations.D: Not recommended for routine asthma treatment.

Instructions

Question 4 & 5 relate to this case

Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Case 2

Andrew is 14 years old and has chronic severe asthma. He has had frequent hospital admissions, in addition to exercise-induced asthma and nocturnal symptoms most days. He uses salbutamol (Ventolin) most days.

He has been prescribed Ventolin (salbutamol) and Flixotide (fluticasone) via a large volume spacer (Volumatic), but does not take his medication regularly as he hates the spacer. When questioned, Andrew is unsure what medications he takes until prompted by his mother.
